attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post. He endorses it and is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: This is an observation about what the DeepSeek results show. 'Possible' describes feasibility, not hedged confidence. Rendering 'get by' as 'competitive AI' is a reasonable gloss, and the 'suggest' framing is kept.

contract.note: The contract asks only whether the results gave evidence for the possibility, which matches 'suggest'. Reading 'get by' as competitive capability and 'top-of-the-line' as Nvidia's best available accelerators is ordinary and fair. Both readings are the evaluator's, not Marcus's.

evidence.note: DeepSeek's own V3 report (Dec 2024) says the model was trained on 2048 H800s and reports competitive benchmark results. It is the developer's account and was not independently audited.
Lenovo's product guide says the H800 has slower NVLink and lower FP64 than the H100, so it sits below the H100. It covers PCIe cards, not DeepSeek's exact cluster.
Nvidia's Nov 2024 post says H200 NVL systems would ship from December, so a higher-end offering existed above the H800 during the period.

reviews.rationale: V3 is a model DeepSeek reported as competitive, and its report says it was trained on H800s, which sit below both the H100 and the newer H200. That gives a reasonable evidential basis for 'suggest it is possible to get by' without top chips. The caveats are that DeepSeek reported its own hardware without an audit, and R1's full hardware is not established. Neither caveat contradicts a suggested possibility.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post. The Davos rumour that follows is separate and is not part of this claim.

semantics.note: The normalised claim faithfully keeps all three conjoined observations: GPT-5 had not arrived, competitors catch up quickly, and there is no obvious moat. All are dated to the time of the post.

contract.note: Marcus named no measure, so the claim is scored on a plain reading. Reading 'quickly' as weeks or months, 'catch up' as broadly comparable ability, and 'moat' as a durable technical edge is ordinary and not stretched for or against him. These are evaluator choices.

evidence.note: DeepSeek's Jan 22, 2025 report says R1 is comparable to o1-1217 on reasoning tasks. This is the developer's own evaluation.
Aider's independent coding test (Jan 24, 2025) found R1+Sonnet beat o1. R1 alone scored below o1, so this is a combined-system result.
The o1 series launched in Sept 2024, which makes the January matches a catch-up of about four months.
OpenAI's o3 posted a large ARC-AGI lead in Dec 2024, but it was an unreleased demonstration only weeks old. That is too recent to show a durable moat.
OpenAI introduced GPT-5 in Aug 2025, which implies it was not out in Jan 2025. The event falls outside the January window, so it is context.

reviews.rationale: GPT-5 was not available in January 2025; it was introduced in August 2025. R1 matched o1 on reasoning within months, and an R1 combination beat o1 on an independent coding test. o3's ARC-AGI lead was a single, unreleased, weeks-old result, which the contract says cannot establish a moat. The limit is that the catch-up evidence is thin: mainly one o1-to-R1 case, not a representative series of comparisons.
